title: Start from the English word you know
summary: Search the dictionary from the English side and read the candidates rather than trusting a translator.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: When you know the idea but not the Chinese word, search from the English side and treat the result as a shortlist, not an answer. Read the full entry for each candidate, including which part of speech it is and what its examples look like, then choose the one whose examples match the sentence you want. Machine translation usually hands you one confident word with no such checks, which is why it teaches the same mistake twice. Keep the rejected candidates in your notes too; knowing why a near-synonym did not fit is a durable piece of learning.

blocks.title: Quick checks before you choose
body: Is it a verb, a noun, or a measure word?
Does an example sentence use it the way you plan to?
Does it take 了 le, 在 zài, or a complement you did not expect?
